notes.gwp-002: AR6 includes climate-carbon feedback. Fossil vs biogenic distinction introduced.
notes.gwp-003: Biogenic methane has slightly lower GWP due to carbon cycle accounting.
notes.gwp-006: Used in R-410A blend. Low-GWP alternative to R-22.
notes.gwp-008: Most widely used automotive refrigerant. Being phased down under Kigali Amendment.
notes.gwp-013: Extremely long atmospheric lifetime. Primary PFC from aluminium smelting.
notes.gwp-016: Highest GWP of any gas measured. Used in electrical switchgear. F-gas regulations apply.
notes.gwp-018: HFC-125/143a/134a (44/52/4%). Common in commercial refrigeration. Being phased down.
notes.gwp-019: HFC-32/125 (50/50%). Standard in air conditioning. R-32 is lower-GWP single-component alternative.
notes.gwp-022: Natural refrigerant with near-zero GWP. Flammable (A3 safety class).
notes.gwp-024: Zero GWP. Toxic and flammable but widely used in industrial refrigeration.

reference.title: GWP Reference Notes
reference.horizonDesc: GWP-100 is the standard for GHG inventories (GHG Protocol, CDP). GWP-20 shows short-term warming impact — methane is 82.5x CO₂ over 20 years vs 29.8x over 100 years.
reference.arDesc: IPCC AR6 (2021) updated GWP values. Most frameworks still accept AR5, but CDP 2025+ and CSRD/ESRS require AR6. Check framework guidance.
reference.kigaliDesc: HFCs are being phased down under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol. Report HFC usage for compliance tracking and transition planning.
